subject: 9170438CF5C0E2D84968B1DE41C36F0F
introduction: The first reading kept here states the order that governs the rest: God’s mercy has preceded His wrath, and His grace His justice. Between that opening and its return at the end, the readings speak of justice in hard terms. They ask how long the oppressed must wait, announce that the tyrant will be seized and recall those who were, counsel the wronged to leave their case to God, and confess in prayer that if God looked with the eye of justice no one would stand. The Psalms, the prophets, the Qur’an and Portia’s speech on mercy belong to this same way of speaking. The quotations set against it ask what such language risks: Edwards shows wrath put first, Ivan Karamazov refuses a justice that is explained only afterwards, Job argues his cause and is commended for it, Jesus forbids reading a calamity as guilt and rebukes disciples who want fire from heaven, and Douglass warns that power concedes nothing to those who only wait.
questions: The readings begin and end by saying that mercy has preceded wrath. How does that order change the way the passages on retribution between them should be read?
The psalmists, Habakkuk and these prayers all ask how long. What is the believer asked to do during the delay?
Several readings say that an oppressor was seized by God. Jesus said those crushed by the tower were no worse than others. Who may read another’s misfortune as a judgment?
The wronged are told to leave injustice to God, and Douglass says power concedes nothing without a demand. Where does trust in divine justice end and the duty to act begin?
Job questioned God and was commended; his friends defended God and were rebuked. What does that suggest about how to speak of justice to someone who is suffering?
Portia says that in the course of justice none of us should see salvation. What follows for how we judge one another?

outside.why: The psalm says the same of the Lord: slow to anger and plenteous in mercy, He has not dealt with us after our sins.
Jonathan Edwards preached a God who holds the sinner over the pit as one holds a spider over the fire. What is changed in a person's religion when wrath is put first and mercy second?
The psalmist asks the same question in the same words: Lord, how long shall the wicked triumph?
The psalm says that justice and judgment are the habitation of God's throne, and that mercy and truth go before His face.
In the parable the last hired are paid as much as the first, and the owner asks whether he may not do what he will with his own.
The elder brother of the prodigal had served for years and saw a feast given to the one who wasted everything. How does grace look to someone who has been given only his due?
Habakkuk begins his book by asking how long he must cry out of violence and not be saved.
In Revelation the souls of the slain cry from beneath the altar: how long, O Lord, dost Thou not judge?
Micah names justice first among the things required: to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly.
The Letter to the Hebrews warns that it is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
The Qur’an says that corruption appears on land and sea because of what human hands have earned, so that they may return.
Isaiah cries woe on those who decree unrighteous decrees and turn aside the needy from judgment.
Deuteronomy commands those who judge in the gates: that which is altogether just shalt thou follow.
Isaiah's servant brings forth judgment to the nations without lifting his voice in the street.
Amos asks that judgment run down as waters and righteousness as a mighty stream.
Paul states the law of requital in a farmer's terms: whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.

Confucius thought that an order kept by punishments teaches people only to avoid them, while one led by virtue gives them a sense of shame. Is reward and punishment the foundation of order or its last resort?

The Preacher observed that because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, people's hearts are set to do evil. Why is the recompense so often delayed, and what does the delay do to those who wait?
Aristotle held that to let law rule is to let God and reason rule, since law is reason unaffected by desire.
Jesus told Peter that all who take the sword shall perish with the sword.
Isaiah hears that God's thoughts are not our thoughts, and His ways higher than ours as the heavens are higher than the earth.

Dostoevsky's Ivan says that even if all were explained at the end he would return his ticket, because the price of that harmony is a child's suffering. Does a justice revealed later answer a wrong suffered now?
Pope summed up this confidence: all partial evil is universal good, and whatever is, is right.
One of Job's friends asks whether mortal man shall be more just than God.
Job himself wished to find God, set his cause in order before Him and fill his mouth with arguments, and in the end he is the one commended. Is it faith or its failure to question what God does?
Abraham reasons with God in the same way: shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?
The Qur’an speaks of a just balance set up on the Day of Resurrection, so that no soul is wronged in anything.
The Qur’an says that God does not wrong anyone even by the weight of an ant, and doubles a good deed.
The seer of Revelation saw the books opened and the dead judged according to their works.
The Qur’an says: deem not that God is unaware of what the wicked do; He only gives them a respite.
The Qur’an also says that there is no compulsion in religion. How do readers of the Qur’an hold that verse together with the verse of the sword that the Báb cites here?
Jesus said that he came not to send peace but a sword, a saying his followers have read as a figure and sometimes as a warrant.
Jeremiah was set over nations to root out and pull down, and also to build and to plant.
Obadiah states the rule of retribution: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee.
Nahum says that the Lord is slow to anger and great in power, and will not at all acquit the wicked.
Paul tells his readers not to avenge themselves, because it is written: vengeance is mine, I will repay.
Ezekiel hears God swear that He has no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn and live. What is the purpose of vengeance as scripture describes it?
Paul asks his readers to behold both the goodness and the severity of God.
Jesus told those who honoured the dead prophets that they were the children of those who killed them.

Julian of Norwich was shown that all shall be well, and all manner of thing shall be well, and could not see how that agreed with the church's teaching on the lost. Can the hope that none is finally shut out be held with passages like this one?
Hobbes quoted the old saying that man is a wolf to man.

Jesus denied that those on whom the tower fell were sinners above their neighbours, and scripture elsewhere denies that children bear their fathers' guilt. How should the suffering of a people be related to the misdeeds of its past?
The Dhammapada says that hatred does not cease by hatred at any time, but by love.
The psalmist saw the wicked in great power, spreading like a green bay tree; he passed by, and he was not.
The writing on Belshazzar's wall said: thou art weighed in the balances and art found wanting.
While the king's boast was still in his mouth a voice said: the kingdom is departed from thee.
Isaiah taunts a fallen king who had said in his heart, I will ascend into heaven: how art thou fallen.
The Preacher saw that time and chance happen to all, and that the wise and the fool die alike. How can one tell a tyrant's fall as judgment from a tyrant's fall as the common lot?
Shelley's king of kings is a shattered face in the desert, with nothing beside remaining.
Jesus said: judge not, that ye be not judged. Who may say of another's misfortune that God has seized him?
Jesus warned that the children of the kingdom themselves may be cast into outer darkness.
The Book of Revelation ends with a warning to anyone who adds to its words or takes away from them.
Hosea says of the faithless that they have sown the wind and shall reap the whirlwind.
In Acts the prison gate opens of its own accord for Peter, and he goes out.
The psalm says that God judges the righteous and is angry with the wicked every day.

The Qur’an says that if God took mankind to task for their wrongdoing He would not leave a living creature on the earth, but He reprieves them. What does it mean that requital comes to some and is withheld from most?
Hannah sings of the Lord who brings low and lifts up, and by whom actions are weighed.
Jeremiah asked God to His face why the way of the wicked prospers. What should be said of the oppressors who die in comfort?
Paul says that the day comes as a thief in the night, when they shall say peace and safety.
When Nineveh took heed, God repented of the evil He had said He would do. What response to a calamity turns it from a punishment into a warning that was heard?
The psalmist admits that his feet had almost slipped when he saw the prosperity of the wicked.
Proverbs advises: say not thou, I will recompense evil; wait on the Lord.
The first letter of Peter says of Christ that when he suffered he threatened not, but committed himself to Him that judges righteously.
Frederick Douglass, who had been a slave, said that power concedes nothing without a demand. When is leaving an injustice to God faith, and when is it permission for the oppressor?
The psalm charges those who judge to defend the poor and fatherless and to deliver them from the hand of the wicked.
Habakkuk is told that the vision is for an appointed time: though it tarry, wait for it.
Isaiah says that God brings princes to nothing, and that the whirlwind takes them away as stubble.
James tells the rich who have heaped up treasure that their gold and silver will be a witness against them.
In the parable of the last judgment the two companies are divided by what they did for the least of these.
The Qur’an has God say in the same breath that He smites whom He will and that His mercy embraces all things. How far does a mercy that embraces all things reach?
The second psalm says that He who sits in the heavens shall laugh at the rulers who take counsel against Him.
The name proclaimed to Moses joins the two: merciful and gracious, and that will by no means clear the guilty.
An angel cries over the great city in Revelation: Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen.
Isaiah cries woe on those who call evil good and good evil.
The Qur’an says of those who schemed against Muhammad: they plot, but God also plots.
Lincoln said of his country's war that if God willed it to continue until every drop drawn by the lash was repaid, the judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether.
Socrates held that it is better to suffer injustice than to do it, since the doer is the one harmed.
Milton prayed after a massacre of villagers in the Alps: avenge, O Lord, thy slaughtered saints.
Jesus told his followers to love their enemies and pray for those who persecute them. How do you read a prayer that God abase His enemies beside that command?
When two disciples wished to call down fire on a village, Jesus rebuked them and said they knew not what manner of spirit they were of. Who may ask for the word of wrath, and against whom?
Isaiah says that the Lord saw there was no judgment, and wondered that there was no intercessor.
The psalm prays that the king be given God's judgments, so that he may judge the poor with justice.
The second letter of Peter explains the forbearance: the Lord is longsuffering, not willing that any should perish.
Jonah was angry when the city he had warned was spared, and God asked whether He should not have pity on it. What should one who longs for the punishment of oppressors learn from Jonah?
Isaiah hears: for a small moment have I forsaken thee, but with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee.
The psalmist asks: if Thou, Lord, shouldest mark iniquities, who shall stand? But there is forgiveness with Thee.
Portia tells Shylock that in the course of justice none of us should see salvation.
The psalmist prays: enter not into judgment with thy servant, for in thy sight shall no man living be justified.
The tax-collector in the parable would not lift his eyes, and said: God be merciful to me a sinner.
Portia says that mercy is not strained, and that it becomes the throned monarch better than his crown.
James puts the precedence of grace over justice in four words: mercy rejoiceth against judgment.
Paul quotes the word to Moses: I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy.
Ezekiel insists that each soul answers for its own deeds, and that the righteousness of the righteous is upon him. How is a God who exalts whom He wills also a God who gives each his due?
John the Baptist said that the axe is laid to the root of the trees.
Micah asks who is a God like this, who retains not His anger for ever because He delights in mercy.
The psalm says that as far as the east is from the west, so far has He removed our transgressions.
Lamentations says it is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed, and they are new every morning.
Habakkuk prays in the middle of the years: in wrath remember mercy.
The psalm says that His anger endures but a moment, and joy comes in the morning.
Malachi promises that the sun of righteousness shall arise with healing in its wings.

romans-vengeance-is-mine.text: Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord

psalm-wicked-in-great-power.text: I have seen the wicked in great power, and spreading himself like a green bay tree. Yet he passed away, and, lo, he was not: yea, I sought him, but he could not be found

psalm-prosperity-of-the-wicked.text: But as for me, my feet were almost gone; my steps had well nigh slipped. For I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked

jeremiah-wherefore-doth-the-wicked-prosp.text: Righteous art thou, O Lord, when I plead with thee: yet let me talk with thee of thy judgments: Wherefore doth the way of the wicked prosper? wherefore are all they happy that deal very treacherously

ecclesiastes-sentence-not-executed-speed.text: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil

psalm-enter-not-into-judgment.text: And enter not into judgment with thy servant: for in thy sight shall no man living be justified

habakkuk-in-wrath-remember-mercy.text: O Lord, I have heard thy speech, and was afraid: O Lord, revive thy work in the midst of the years, in the midst of the years make known; in wrath remember mercy

isaiah-for-a-small-moment.text: For a small moment have I forsaken thee; but with great mercies will I gather thee. In a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment; but with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith the Lord thy Redeemer

hosea-how-shall-i-give-thee-up.text: How shall I give thee up, Ephraim? how shall I deliver thee, Israel? how shall I make thee as Admah? how shall I set thee as Zeboim? mine heart is turned within me, my repentings are kindled together. I will not execute the fierceness of mine anger, I will not return to destroy Ephraim: for I am God, and not man; the Holy One in the midst of thee: and I will not enter into the city

romans-goodness-and-severity.text: Behold therefore the goodness and severity of God: on them which fell, severity; but toward thee, goodness, if thou continue in his goodness: otherwise thou also shalt be cut off

nahum-slow-to-anger.text: The Lord is slow to anger, and great in power, and will not at all acquit the wicked: the Lord hath his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet

psalm-how-long-shall-the-wicked-triumph.text: O Lord God, to whom vengeance belongeth; O God, to whom vengeance belongeth, shew thyself. Lift up thyself, thou judge of the earth: render a reward to the proud. Lord, how long shall the wicked, how long shall the wicked triumph

isaiah-how-art-thou-fallen.text: How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations! For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north: I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High. Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit

hebrews-fearful-thing.text: For we know him that hath said, Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord. And again, The Lord shall judge his people. It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God

deuteronomy-justice-shalt-thou-follow.text: That which is altogether just shalt thou follow, that thou mayest live, and inherit the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee

psalm-not-dealt-with-us.text: The Lord is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy. He will not always chide: neither will he keep his anger for ever. He hath not dealt with us after our sins; nor rewarded us according to our iniquities

psalm-justice-and-judgment.text: Justice and judgment are the habitation of thy throne: mercy and truth shall go before thy face

obadiah-as-thou-hast-done.text: For the day of the Lord is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head

exodus-pharaoh-hardened.text: And in very deed for this cause have I raised thee up, for to shew in thee my power; and that my name may be declared throughout all the earth

proverbs-say-not-i-will-recompense.text: Say not thou, I will recompense evil; but wait on the Lord, and he shall save thee

matthew-judge-not.text: Judge not, that ye be not judged. For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again

job-shall-mortal-man-be-more-just.text: Shall mortal man be more just than God? shall a man be more pure than his maker

job-i-would-order-my-cause.text: Oh that I knew where I might find him! that I might come even to his seat! I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments. I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me

psalm-judgeth-the-righteous.text: God judgeth the righteous, and God is angry with the wicked every day

quran-wrongeth-not-an-atoms-weight.text: Lo! Allah wrongeth not even of the weight of an ant; and if there is a good deed, He will double it and will give (the doer) from His presence an immense reward.

quran-scales-of-justice.text: And We set a just balance for the Day of Resurrection so that no soul is wronged in aught. Though it be of the weight of a grain of mustard seed, We bring it. And We suffice for reckoners.
